correctness.rationale: For the repaired theorem, the one-rate closed Epperson criterion has κ_p=2√(p−1)/|p−2| with the standard Gaussian and generator −∂²+x∂. The product extension is contractive by successive coordinate applications and Fubini, and restricting to functions of one coordinate proves necessity. For 0<t<t_b the line (as,bs) modulo π is dense. A period of the slice gives equality of the product indicator and its translate on this line; the difference is locally constant off the union of the original and translated boundaries. It must vanish there by density, and the boundaries have Haar measure zero. The two window measures are positive, so marginal integration transfers invariance to each arc. In Haar probability measure on R/πZ, the first coefficient of the arc [−δ,δ] is sin(2δ)/π, strictly positive for 0<δ<π/2, forcing the corresponding translation to vanish modulo π. Thus both aτ and bτ lie in πZ, giving τ=0 by irrationality. At t_b the faster window is already full, and the nontrivial slower window has exactly period group (π/a)Z until t_a; from t_a onward every imaginary time is allowed. Equality is included by closed boundedness. As an independent check, p=4,a=1,b=√2 gives κ_p=√3 and thresholds (log 3)/(2√2) and (log 3)/2 with the predicted intervening period π. The frozen density assertions are correct but removed as a contribution: under irrationality the torus window measure is the product by null-boundary equidistribution, and for coprime rational rates distinct zeros are separated by at least π/(mnλ), so under the sum-of-half-widths bound only the common-zero overlap remains. The frozen density diagnostic was inspected but not executed and does not test exact periods.

This narrower theorem passes on the inspected evidence; this is not a pass for the original density thesis.

value.rationale: The repaired theorem identifies the exact real smoothing depth at which an aperiodic region develops periodic imaginary-time sections, the least shift needed to reduce admissibility to one period, and when that test becomes unnecessary. Global aperiodicity alone cannot answer this slice question. The nontrivial exclusion below the faster-rate threshold makes the onset sharp rather than merely a sufficient regime. The prior density classification is not credited as new value.
